author: human
request:
Feature request: the vet list answers "which specialties does this vet hold",
but staff also ask the inverse — "which vets hold this specialty". Two
product decisions come with it, made here as the product owner:

- A read-only specialty view of the existing directory is in scope; managing
  veterinarians or specialties stays out of scope as before (non-goal NG-2
  is unchanged).
- The page is reachable by its URL alone: no navigation entry and no link
  from another page is part of this request. A visible entry point may come
  as a follow-up request.

Add a specialty directory page:

- GET /specialties.html lists every specialty the clinic knows by its stored
  name, each with the veterinarians holding it.
- Each veterinarian is shown by full name: first name, then last name (for
  example "Helen Leary").
- A veterinarian holding no specialty appears under no specialty; the page
  lists specialties, not the full vet roster.
- All specialties render on one page — no pagination.

Cover the new behavior with tests.

These are all the product decisions; no further product answer will come
during the work. Where a choice still seems open, take the narrowest reading
consistent with this request and record the open question rather than
waiting.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: The specialty view is a second read surface over the vet feature package and needs no new pattern. Three existing patterns cover it end to end: the lookup-entity repository (PetTypeRepository), the server-rendered controller plus Thymeleaf template under the shared layout fragment (VetController + vets/vetList.html), and the Value object row of the pattern catalog's In force list. The one adjustment durable memory did not already carry is the inversion: Specialty holds no association back to Vet, so the specialty-to-veterinarian mapping is assembled in memory from two repository reads rather than read from the mapping. That assembly is a new read-model type, SpecialtyHolders, recorded in system-design.md Contracts along with SpecialtyRepository and SpecialtyController; the Vet, Specialty and VetRepository rows now also cite REQ-VET-003. No ADR: the placement follows the pattern catalog as written and reverses cheaply. Basis for the covering claim is grep plus direct reads of the vet package and the templates directory (the IDE oracle is not connected here), which is the weaker basis: Specialty.java is empty beyond its mapping and no file under src/main matches /specialties.
integration_points: GET /specialties.html is a new read-only route in the vet package; it takes no path variable, no query parameter and binds no form, so it adds no request-bound type and no new trust boundary
SpecialtyRepository is a new persistence gateway for the Specialty lookup entity, returning specialties in name order; it is the only way a specialty no veterinarian holds reaches the page

SpecialtyController reads veterinarians through the existing VetRepository.findAll(), which is @Cacheable("vets") and eagerly fetches specialties, so no new repository method on Vet and no lazy-initialization exposure with spring.jpa.open-in-view disabled
SpecialtyHolders is a pure in-memory assembly over the two collections: no Spring import, no repository reference, constructed and asserted in a plain unit test

fragments/layout.html is NOT edited: the new template consumes the layout for standard navigation (REQ-SYS-001) and passes a menu value matching no menu item, so navigation renders with nothing marked active and no page gains a link to the view

the view is a new HTML output of already-public data: specialty names and veterinarian names, which /vets.html already serves to any caller; read-only, no mutation, no management-endpoint change (security-principles.md § Realization, Widening the exposed surface)

patterns.description: lookup-entity repository returning rows in name order via an explicit @Query; SpecialtyRepository mirrors it for Specialty
server-rendered controller shape: constructor-injected repository, @GetMapping, model attribute, view name returned
template head: th:replace of fragments/layout with the body and a menu key; specialtyList.html copies this line with a menu value that matches no menu item
@WebMvcTest slice with MockMvc and @MockitoBean repository; SpecialtyControllerTests follows it, and the assembly logic gets a plain unit test without Spring
Value object row (In force): SpecialtyHolders is an immutable record pairing one Specialty with its veterinarians, defensively copying the list

risks.risk: Object-identity grouping silently produces an empty page. VetRepository.findAll() is @Cacheable and each repository method opens its own read-only transaction, so the Specialty instances reached through Vet.getSpecialties() are different objects from those SpecialtyRepository returns. The model superclasses override no equals or hashCode (src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/model/BaseEntity.java), so equality is object identity and Set.contains or List.indexOf will not match
risks.mitigation: Group by Specialty.getId() (a Map<Integer, List<Vet>> keyed by identifier), never by object identity. architecture-principles.md § Domain Core: aggregates reference each other by identity. Recorded in system-design.md § Contracts, invariants paragraph

risks.risk: Placing the grouping and ordering inside SpecialtyController would be a fresh violation of the Web controller row, which the recorded deviation explicitly does not extend to new rules, and would make the behavior reachable only through MockMvc
risks.mitigation: SpecialtyHolders owns the grouping and both orderings as a static, Spring-free assembly; SpecialtyController binds nothing, delegates, and selects the view (docs/architecture-principles.md § Pattern Catalog, Web controller row and § Design Validation Checklist)

risks.risk: A hard-coded string in the new template, or a new message key added only to messages.properties, fails I18nPropertiesSyncTest and breaches REQ-LANG-002
risks.mitigation: Prefer the existing keys the base bundle already carries in all locales: specialties, vets, name, none. A genuinely new key must be added to messages.properties and to all nine translated bundles; messages_en.properties is skipped by the sync test on purpose. Specialty names and veterinarian names render as stored data and take no key (docs/prd.md REQ-VET-003 edge case 5)

risks.risk: Two veterinarians sharing a last and first name leave the order undetermined, since neither repository read carries an ORDER BY over veterinarians and the acceptance criterion demands a stable rather than arbitrary order
risks.mitigation: Sort veterinarians by last name, then first name, then identifier; sort specialties by name in the repository query. Deterministic for every input (docs/prd.md REQ-VET-003 edge cases 1 and 4)

risks.risk: Marking SpecialtyRepository @Cacheable would extend a caching posture whose invalidation is an unsettled open question
risks.mitigation: Leave the new repository uncached. docs/system-design.md § Open Questions from the Survey, item 5 (vet cache invalidation)

notes: Placement deviates from the prd-entry file_targets, which named VetController. A /specialties.html handler is a different resource, not a second representation of the vet list, and the owner package already demonstrates one controller per surface (OwnerController, PetController, VisitController). docs/architecture-principles.md § Naming requires a web controller prefixed by the domain noun or the surface it serves, so the route lands in a new SpecialtyController inside the existing vet package. No new package, so the acyclic package graph is unchanged. Name SpecialtyHolders is taken from docs/ubiquitous-language.md, which defines a Specialty as held by zero or more Veterinarians; it avoids the recorded Vets collision and carries no prohibited suffix. No ubiquitous-language change is needed. Design writes this dispatch: docs/system-design.md package-structure vet line, the Contracts invariants paragraph, three new Contracts rows, and REQ-VET-003 added to the Vet, Specialty and VetRepository rows. Open questions carried forward rather than consulted, per the owner's standing instruction: (1) whether the stable order is meant to be alphabetical, which this design settles as last name then first name without product confirmation; (2) whether a test should assert the absence of a link to the view across templates, which would pin the last acceptance criterion mechanically the way I18nPropertiesSyncTest pins REQ-LANG-002 - left to the implementer and the test reviewer. No design-doc-autofix records exist in the log, so the autofix audit found nothing to judge.

author: security-reviewer
recommendations: Supply chain not verified against the NVD in this pass: build.gradle is unchanged (no new or upgraded dependency), and the OWASP dependency-check plugin is not configured, so no NVD match ran. The resolved framework baseline stays Spring Boot 4.1.1. A human or CI closes this check; it is a pre-existing project condition, not a defect this change introduces.

The route is reachable by anyone who knows the address while nothing links to it (PRD acceptance criterion). That is not access control, and a demonstration is read and copied. It exposes no data beyond what /vets.html and /vets already publish, so it does not leave the application weaker than the baseline in docs/system-design.md#security-context; worth a sentence in the docs if the unlinked-ness is ever mistaken for confidentiality.

The page renders every specialty and every veterinarian with no pagination (a stated requirement) and vetRepository.findAll() is the baseline unbounded read already used by /vets. Response size is therefore bounded only by table size; with no write endpoint (NG-2) an attacker has no path to grow it, so this is a note rather than a finding.
approved_aspects: XSS: every request-reachable value on src/main/resources/templates/vets/specialtyList.html renders through th:text (specialty name at :18, veterinarian names at :21). No th:utext, no inline JavaScript, no remote resource, no href built from data; the swept grep for utext and Thymeleaf preprocessing (__${...}__) across the new template and the new Java files returned nothing. Escaping matches the neighbouring vets/vetList.html exactly, so the Cross-site scripting row of docs/security-principles.md holds.

Injection into data access: SpecialtyRepository.findSpecialties() is a static JPQL string with no parameters and no concatenation; nothing request-derived reaches it. GET /specialties.html binds no path variable, no query parameter and no form, so the endpoint introduces no request-bound type, no mass-assignment surface and no new trust boundary.

Exposed surface: the new route exposes only specialty names and veterinarian names, both already public at /vets.html and /vets, plus specialty rows no veterinarian holds. The endpoint is recorded in docs/system-design.md, satisfying the 'Widening the exposed surface' row; management-endpoint exposure is untouched.

Pattern consistency: SpecialtyRepository extends JpaRepository like the cited lookup-entity neighbour owner/PetTypeRepository, so the CRUD surface is the baseline shape rather than a widening. Spring Data REST is not on the classpath, so the inherited mutators have no HTTP surface.

Concurrency and shared state: SpecialtyController is a stateless singleton holding only two injected repositories. SpecialtyHolders.assemble reads the @Cacheable("vets") Vet graph without mutating it (Vet.getSpecialties() returns a fresh sorted stream result) and builds its own lists, so no cached instance is mutated across requests. The record's compact constructor defensive-copies via List.copyOf.

No credentials, tokens, or secrets added anywhere in the change set; no logging, no file or stream I/O, no shell execution, no serialization, no randomness, and no system /tmp usage in the new production or test files (verified by grep over the new files).

author: test-reviewer

findings.description: SpecialtyRepository.findSpecialties() carries a hand-written JPQL @Query ("SELECT specialty FROM Specialty specialty ORDER BY specialty.name") that never executes against a real database anywhere in the suite. SpecialtyControllerTests mocks the repository entirely and SpecialtyHoldersTests is a plain unit test that never touches it. The design-block explicitly models this repository on PetTypeRepository, and PetTypeRepository's analogous findPetTypes() query IS exercised with real I/O against the seeded H2 data in ClinicServiceTests (src/test/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/service/ClinicServiceTests.java, e.g. lines 149, 168). A typo or mapping error in the new query (wrong entity name, wrong property path) would pass every test in this slice and only surface at runtime. This is a real coverage gap against the codebase's own established convention for lookup-entity repositories, not an invented expectation - testing-principles.md Mocking Policy requires real I/O for integration coverage of this kind.
findings.fix: Add a @Transactional integration test to ClinicServiceTests (or a same-shape new test class) that autowires the real SpecialtyRepository, calls findSpecialties() against the seeded H2 data (radiology, surgery, dentistry - src/main/resources/db/h2/data.sql), and asserts the real result set and its name order, mirroring the shouldFind... tests already written for PetTypeRepository and VetRepository in that class.

findings.description: theSpecialtyHoldingShouldRefuseMutationOfItsVeterinarians constructs the record under test directly with `new SpecialtyHolders(...)` instead of going through a suite factory, unlike every other test in the file which builds its fixtures through the specialty()/vet() factories. testing-principles.md Test Data Construction requires production types be constructed only behind test-owned factory methods.
findings.fix: Add a small factory, e.g. `aSpecialtyHolding(Specialty specialty, List<Vet> veterinarians)`, and use it here instead of the raw constructor call.

author: change-grader

blast_radius.note: Nine files in one module, and no existing production code is modified at all - the four production files are new, the only edits to existing files are two docs and one added test method. No sensitive paths, nothing under build or config, and the new route is additive, so no existing behavior has a path to change.

semantic_surprise.note: The one non-obvious choice is that SpecialtyHolders.assemble matches holders by identifier rather than object equality, and that is deliberate and defended: BaseEntity inherits identity equality and VetRepository.findAll() is cached, so the two reads return distinct instances for the same row. It is documented in the javadoc and pinned by a test that constructs two Specialty objects for the same id. The repository mirrors PetTypeRepository and the template mirrors vetList.html line for line; no inverted operator, no boundary shift, no silent behavior change anywhere.

test_adequacy.note: The tests assert outcomes rather than restate the implementation. The controller tests drive real MVC dispatch and real Thymeleaf rendering and assert against the rendered HTML, including the negatives - a vet holding no specialty is absent, a specialty nobody holds renders the none label, twelve specialties render with no page-link query string, and a filesystem walk over every template asserts nothing links the route. The hand-written JPQL now executes against seeded H2 in ClinicServiceTests, which closes the round-1 gap and would fail on a wrong entity name or property path.

reviewer_hedging.note: The security reviewer approved with three recommendations rather than cleanly. One is an unrun check it explicitly hands to a human or CI - no NVD supply-chain match ran, since the OWASP plugin is not configured. Two describe properties of what ships: the route is reachable by anyone who knows the address while nothing links to it, which the reviewer warns is not access control and suggested documenting, and that sentence was not written; and the page is unpaginated over an unbounded findAll. Each is framed as a note rather than a defect, and the round-2 silence from the security and doc reviewers is the fix-delta plan scoping them out, not a hedge.

scope_deviation.note: The changed files match the design-block primary paths exactly, plus the docs sync and the test the reviewer asked for. Zero design revisions and zero consultations, and the lone build retry is a planned checkpoint handoff rather than a gate failure, so the row's retry count overstates the trouble. Both open questions were recorded in the PRD rather than answered, which is what the intake instructed, and the no-navigation-entry decision is enforced by a test.

rationale: Nothing in the code needs a careful read: additive, contained, and the one subtle choice is documented and tested. What deserves a look is the security reviewer's three recommendations - an unrun supply-chain check, and an unlinked, unauthenticated, unpaginated public page whose unlinked-ness it warned must not be mistaken for confidentiality. Read those, then merge.
